subject: fix(fa3): no NaN embeddings with fa_skip_kv_cache under piecewise CUDA graph (#27343)
pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes NaN embeddings emitted by the `fa_skip_kv_cache` embedding fast path (added in #21971) when **piecewise CUDA graph** is enabled. ~40% of **short** embedding inputs came back as fully-NaN vectors; long inputs were unaffected.

## Root cause

`fa_skip_kv_cache` serves attention with `flash_attn_varlen_func` on raw K/V. Under a piecewise CUDA graph the model forward runs at a **padded token-bucket size**, so the query tensor `q` has more rows (`B`) than `cu_seqlens_q` covers (`N`, the real token count).

`flash_attn_varlen_func` requires `q.shape[0] == cu_seqlens_q[-1]`. With `N < B` that contract is violated, and the boundary query block corrupts the **last real token's** output. Embedding models use LAST-token pooling, so that corrupted row *is* the returned embedding → NaN.

Only short inputs are affected: long inputs fill the top bucket (no padding / the boundary lands harmlessly), while short inputs get padded into a small bucket, placing the last real token right at the corrupting boundary. It reproduces only with the FA3 backend (the flashinfer backend is already piecewise-padding-aware), and is independent of `--prefill-only-disable-kv-cache` (it is gated on the embedding config, not that flag).

## Fix

Append the padded tail `[N, B)` as a **dummy, self-attending segment** so `cu_seqlens = [0, …, N, B]` and `q.shape[0] == cu_seqlens_q[-1]` holds again. The real-token segments are untouched (their attention is unchanged), and the padding rows get valid, isolated self-attention instead of reading uninitialized memory. This mirrors how the flashinfer backend reserves a dummy request for piecewise padding.

## Validation

H100, Qwen3-0.6B embedding model (fp16), fa3 + piecewise:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| previously-NaN short inputs | 81/81 NaN | **0** |
| overall NaN | ~40% of short | **0/1000** |
| cosine vs non-piecewise (correct) path | — | **mean 0.9999987, min 0.9999946** (all 1000 ≥ 0.99999) |

So the fix removes the NaN *and* leaves correct embeddings bit-for-bit equivalent.

## Test

Adds `test/registered/prefill_only/test_fa_skip_kv_cache_piecewise_nan.py`:
- `test_no_nan_with_piecewise` — short inputs (~1–150 toke …[truncated]

subject: [misc] Fix tool-call index, graph padded-row count, and prefill-graph input_embeds refresh (#39574)
pr_body:
## Summary

Five independent fixes in the OpenAI chat server, the CUDA graph runners, and the MoE runners. Each is one or two commits and stands on its own.

## Changes

**1. Non-streaming `tool_calls[i].index` is the call ordinal.**
`_process_tool_calls` numbered calls by the detector's `tool_index`, which for most detectors is the tool's position in the request. Two calls to the same tool therefore both got `index=0`, while the streaming deltas number them 0 and 1. The non-streaming path now enumerates the parsed calls. Regression test added in `test_serving_chat.py`.

**2. `num_token_non_padded` is only handed out when it is maintained.**
The decode graph runner allocated the `num_token_non_padded` slot unconditionally, wrote it at capture, and refreshed it at replay only under expert parallelism. Without EP the static ForwardBatch carried a stale capture-time count, while eager batches carry `None` (`ForwardBatch.init_new` only fills it under EP). `DecodeInputBuffers.create` and the dummy-run buffers now allocate the slot only when `enable_num_token_non_padded()`; the capture-time writes are guarded. Graph and eager batches now follow the same rule: no count unless it is live.

**3. The standard MoE path masks padded rows like the a2a path.**
`DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal` and `forward_normal_dual_stream` pass `forward_batch.num_token_non_padded` into top-k, as `forward_deepep` already does. With EP and the standard dispatcher, padded rows of a CUDA graph batch are now routed to expert id -1 instead of real experts, which also keeps them out of the expert-distribution statistics. Without EP the count is `None` and routing is unchanged. The dual-stream variant is additionally skipped inside a breakable CUDA graph capture, matching the guard the hc path already has.

**4. Prefill CUDA graph replay refreshes the `input_embeds` slot from `input_ids`.**
When the outer forward calls the captured stack without `input_embeds`, the replay closure previously left the slot untouched and the graph read the previous batch's embeddings. It now computes them from `input_ids` via `get_input_embeddings()`.

**5. Deferred finalize accepts fp32 expert weights.**

subject: [Bugfix] Handle Asym W4A16 (ConchLinearKernel) for CT (#33200)
pr_body:
Fix ConchLinearKernel to correctly handle asymmetric quantization (uint4/uint8 with explicit zero points) on ROCm.

## Purpose

Root cause: The Conch kernel expects unpacked zero points with shape (K//G, N), but vLLM was passing packed zeros with shape (N//pack, K//G). This caused out-of-bounds memory access resulting in: `HIP error: an illegal memory access was encountered`

The fix unpacks the zero points from packed int32 format and reorders them to match the kernel's expected layout. The unpacking logic now correctly handles both 4-bit (8 values/int32) and 8-bit (4 values/int32) quantization based on the weight type's bit width.

## Test Plan
```
vllm bench latency --model RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16 --num-iters 1
```

## Test Result
Crashes before this PR, succeeds with this PR.

Compared outputs with Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ (same base model, AWQ quantization). Both models produce identical correct answers on 8 test questions (100% match).

Note: No unit test added - we could not find a small asymmetric CT W4A16 model. 
Note: The fix also handles asymmetric uint8, but we could not find such a model on HuggingFace to validate (all W8A16 CT models found are symmetric).

subject: [Misc] Fixes and Optimizations for DeepEP + DeepGEMM combination. (#19298)
pr_body:
## Purpose
### Issue1:
  The engine fails to initialize with DeepseekR1 + data-parallel-size 32 + expert-parallel + VLLM_ALL2ALL_BACKEND="deepep_high_throughput" + VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1

#### Cause:
  During profile runs we execute model forward pass on all GPUs with maximum batch size. We do this with dummy input_ids all set to zeros. This has an effect of routing all tokens from all GPUs to a specific set of experts / GPU Ranks in the All2All dispatch call. The GPU receiving all the tokens has an enormous batch-size to process. The GPUs OOM as a result.

### Issue2:
   The engine fails to initialize with DeepseekR1 + data-parallel-size 128 + expert-parallel + VLLM_ALL2ALL_BACKEND="deepep_low_latency" + VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1

subject: [Fix] Correct W4AFP8 DeepEP scaling and mode-specific dtypes (#33669)
pr_body:
## Motivation

W4AFP8 with DeepEP had two independent failures in the same normal/prefill path.

First, `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal` called `deepep_post_reorder_triton_kernel` without the required `routed_scaling_factor`, causing the original first-request `TypeError` in #33660. The model forward applies routed scaling after the cross-rank DeepEP combine, so this rank-local reduction must receive the neutral value `1.0`; using the model factor here would scale twice.

After the first fix, the reporter reproduced a second failure on 4xH200: DeepEP `intranode.cu:926` reported `Unsupported type`. That line is the normal **combine** dtype switch, not an INT4-weight dispatch site; DeepEP only transports activations and its normal combine accepts BF16. The actual problem was SGLang's dtype selection:

- W4AFP8 normal/prefill requantizes BF16 activations with checkpoint static scales, so its DeepEP payload must remain BF16.
- W4AFP8 low-latency/decode consumes DeepEP FP8 activations together with per-token-group scales, so that payload must remain FP8.
- With `--deepep-mode auto`, the previous global default selected FP8 for both implementations. The normal W4AFP8 path discarded the returned FP8 scale; a zero-token expert rank then returned an FP8 tensor directly to DeepEP's BF16-only normal combine, producing the reported assertion. Globally forcing BF16 would fix prefill but break low-latency decode.

Fixes #33660.

## Modifications

- Pass neutral `routed_scaling_factor=1.0` to the W4AFP8 DeepEP-normal post-reorder kernel.
- Let each concrete DeepEP implementation resolve a mode-specific dispatcher dtype.
- Configure W4AFP8 as normal=`bf16`, low-latency=`fp8`, including `auto` mode and TBO wrappers through the existing dispatcher configuration propagation.
- Add explicit guards for invalid normal and low-latency payloads, avoiding silent scale loss.
- Add CPU regressions for the kernel argument, per-mode dtype resolution, zero-token normal behavior, and missing low-latency scales.

## Accuracy Tests

The original routed-scale regression was run in the H20 SGLang image and passed before this update. The issue reporter independently confirmed that it fixes the ori …[truncated]

- eplb: fall back to identity mapping when a layer id exceeds the physical expert map (draft workers can query more MoE layers than the target-sized map covers)
- deepseek_v4 norm-rope kernel: skip rows with a negative out_loc sentinel instead of writing out of bounds
- trtllm_mha page-table kernel: clamp the SWA gather index into full_to_swa bounds
- forward_batch_info: guard lora_ids extend when None; skip next_token_logits truncation when a forward returns hidden states only
- ParallelLMHead: forward enable_tp to VocabParallelEmbedding
- one_batch_server: read spec metrics from all internal states (multi-DP servers report them on non-zero ranks)
- hf config registry: register the gemma4_unified alias so AutoConfig resolves the existing model type
- model_runner: draft workers with multi-stage models read num_stages for the layer count

subject: Fix the router GEMM inaccuracy when using _front_w in Kimi-K3 (#33764)
pr_body:
## Problem

The Kimi-K3 MoE layer computes the router logits in bf16. The router then
selects the experts from these bf16 logits. The selection is not accurate.

Other implementations use fp32 for this GEMM:

- vLLM sets `out_dtype=torch.float32` on its gate
- the SGLang EP front (`moe_front.fused_front`) uses `out_dtype=torch.float32`

Measurement with the layer-1 gate weight and the fp32 correction bias:

- 5.27% of the tokens get a different top-16 expert set
- 0.33% of the routed weight goes to different experts (mean); the p99 is 6.4%

Previously, as https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29783 shows in GLM-5.2, this is not safe, and can drop the SWE-Bench Verified score by 79 -> 67. In fact since this path is gated by num_tokens, it will be really difficult to diagnose bugs in the future (when running evals quickly with large batch sizes, vs real world use at small batch sizes)

## The `_front_w` fusion

Three projections in the MoE layer read the same `hidden_states`:

| projection | weight shape at TP8 |
|---|---|
| `shared_experts.gate_up_proj` | `[1536, 7168]` |
| `gate` (the router) | `[896, 7168]` |
| `routed_expert_down_proj` | `[3584, 7168]` |

`_merge_front_weights()` concatenates the three weights along the row axis into
one tensor, `_front_w [6016, 7168]`. One GEMM then replaces three GEMMs. Each
module keeps a view of the merged tensor, so the memory does not increase.

```
hidden_states [M, 7168] --> _front_w [6016, 7168] --> fused [M, 6016]
                                                        |
      cols    0:1536  gate_up  --> SiTU --> shared down_proj
      cols 1536:2432  logits   --> router (sigmoid + bias + top-16)
      cols 2432:6016  latent   --> mxfp8 quant --> trtllm-gen MoE
```

The fusion saves 11-16 us for each MoE layer. The fusion also causes the problem. `fused` is one tensor, and one tensor has one dtype. Two of the three consumers need bf16 (SiTU, MXFP8 quant). Thus the router got bf16, which works functionally but not numerically correct.

## The fix

The GEMM writes fp32. The two other consumers read fp32 directly. No cast pass
and no new kernel are necessary.

subject: [torch.compile] Fix RMSNorm + quant fusion in the non-cutlass-fp8 case, rename RedundantReshapesPass to NoopEliminationPass (#10902)
pr_body:
This PR fixes the `fp8` case, when `cutlass_mm` is not available. It contains the following fixes:
- Removes the padding for `fp8` `torch._scaled_mm`  in the `torch.compile` case, as branch specialization might not work correctly, and it makes fusion difficult.
- Implements redundant `slice` and `slice_scatter` elimination, which is implemented in PyTorch but does not cover all cases. It renames the `RedundantReshapesPass` to `NoopEliminationPass`.
- Minor custom pass improvements.

This PR is a pre-requisite PR to #10836, which enables `torch.compile` on AMD and uses the non-cutlass-fp8 path.

pr_body:
DeepSeek V4 Pro Base FP8 routed MoE needs the model-provided SwiGLU clamp limit to be applied before the second expert GEMM. Without this clamp, DSV4 Pro Base produces garbled outputs and very low eval quality.

This PR patches FP8 MoE backends ('auto' and 'triton') as the Base model's moe experts are FP8.

After this PR, we saw mmlu pro bench has macro 0.7409 / micro 0.7298, which matches model card.

Related PR for instr model's FP4 path (#42287, #42541)

subject: [Bug] Forward fixed_split_size in SWA / cross-attention paths of FlashInfer backend (#26412)
pr_body:
## Bug

`--enable-deterministic-inference` sets `prefill_split_tile_size` — the FlashInfer knob that pins split-K reduction order so attention output is batch-invariant — and threads it through the `update()` chain as `fixed_split_size` (plus `disable_split_kv` on the decode side). But three of the four `update_*` leaf methods in `FlashInferIndicesUpdater{Decode,Prefill}` silently drop these values before calling `call_begin_forward()`:

- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterDecode.update_sliding_window`
- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterDecode.update_cross_attention`
- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_sliding_window`
- `FlashInferIndicesUpdaterPrefill.update_cross_attention`

Only `update_single_wrapper` (full-attention path) forwarded them correctly.

## Impact

Models with sliding-window attention or cross-attention take the SWA / cross-attn path on every layer, so `fixed_split_size` never reaches the FlashInfer kernel. FlashInfer then auto-picks split sizes, and the split-K reduction order depends on total batch tokens. Result: attention output (and downstream logp) drifts across batch shapes / batch composition, in spite of `--enable-deterministic-inference`.

Models without SWA/cross-attention (e.g. Qwen3-8B in the default deterministic-inference CI) take `update_single_wrapper` and are unaffected, which is why existing CI passes today. The bug only surfaces on SWA / cross-attention models.

Verified on an internal SWA model setup with `python -m sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode prefix --n-start 10 --n-trials 10` against a live server launched with `--attention-backend flashinfer --enable-deterministic-inference`:

- **Before:** prefix length 2048 → `Unique samples: 6` (text-level failure too), 22/43 logp mismatches; lengths 511 / 4097 also drift in logp.
- **After:** all 4 prefix lengths → `Unique samples: 1`, `✓✓✓ Logprobs are identical across all batch sizes! ✓✓✓`.

## Fix

Add `fixed_split_size=fixed_split_size` (and `disable_split_kv=disable_split_kv` on the decode side) to the `call_begin_forward()` invocation inside each of the four affected methods. Behavior with `--enable-deterministic-inference` off is unchanged — the value passed in is `None`.
